data.narrative:
Cellino, a Series A biotech company founded by Nabiha Saklayen and Marinna Madrid, has raised approximately $125M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method here. Using total capital raised ($125M) as a valuation proxy and applying a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-round progression, the method implies a post-money valuation of $250M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied without disclosed revenue; the Biotech & Health sector median trades at 6.6x P/S across the three public comparables, but Cellino's revenue is not on file. Peer-median comparison is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-set peers meeting stage and tier filters.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $212M to $288M, centered on $250M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the actual revenue profile (needed to anchor against public multiples), the precise capital structure and any secondary transactions, and whether the 2.0x multiplier appropriately reflects Cellino's risk profile relative to sector norms. Additional disclosure of financials or recent term sheets would substantially narrow this range.
